text: Low-altitude stability and propulsion responsiveness testing with SkyLane-350. Operating close to the ground provides a demanding environment to evaluate the aircraft’s hover stability, control response and propulsion performance. During the test, we verify how quickly and precisely the propulsion system responds to flight controller commands while maintaining a stable position and altitude. These tests are an important part of validating the complete VTOL control loop - from sensors and flight control algorithms to motor response and propulsion dynamics. title: Rinata Ilyubayeva
text: Why did Network School choose Kazakhstan over 10+ countries? A new conversation with Balaji Srinivasan has just premiered across Trusted Kazakhstan, Astana Hub, and Network State Podcast. Network School is building a global community for people who want to learn tech, work remotely, build companies, and live alongside other ambitious people. Kazakhstan is set to become one of the first major global hubs for this model. In the conversation, Balaji Srinivasan, founder of Network School and former CTO of Coinbase, joins Rinata Ilyubayeva , Managing Director at Astana Hub, and host Thorsten Gutmann to discuss why Kazakhstan stood out among more than 10 countries considered for Network School’s expansion. The discussion goes beyond the decision itself. It explores: • why Astana can become a destination for global tech talent • how digital nomads can contribute to Kazakhstan’s innovation ecosystem • new approaches to education and lifelong learning • how global and local talent can build companies together • Kazakhstan’s growing focus on AI, emerging technologies, and new industries • what the cities and communities of the future could look like One of the central ideas of the conversation is simple: Kazakhstan has the opportunity not only to attract global talent, but to create an environment where people can build, scale, and take tech to international markets. For us at Astana Hub, this is also part of a broader ambition: to make Kazakhstan a place where international founders, engineers, creators, and investors can connect with local talent and build globally competitive tech businesses. Watch the full conversation: https://lnkd.in/eCDdXhGU Join Network School: https://ns.com/ Join the opening of Network School in Astana on September 2: https://luma.com/nskz Meet the global tech community at AI & Digital Bridge, October 1-3 in Astana: https://lnkd.in/d8j2HPmf
author: Rinata Ilyubayeva

title: Robert Kleist
text: The opening of Saildrone’s EU headquarters in Copenhagen represents much more than a new office. It is part of a long-term commitment to build the people, operations, partnerships, and industrial capacity needed to support autonomous maritime operations across Europe. At Quintus Bastion, we were honored to mark that next chapter alongside Defence Industry Attaché, His Royal Highness Brigadier General Prince Joachim of Denmark; The Honorable Dale R. Marks; Erik Balck Sørensen of EIFO ; Saildrone Founder and CEO Richard Jenkins; our European Managing Director Robert Kleist ; and customers, partners, and members of the Saildrone team. As the speakers reflected throughout the day, building sovereign European capability does not mean working in isolation. It means bringing together European manufacturing and technology, strong transatlantic relationships, public and private investment, and proven autonomous systems to strengthen maritime security and resilience. Our ambition is clear: to build the European capability to manufacture, deploy, operate, and support Saildrone USVs from the region, for the region.
author: Robert Kleist

title: Sachin Jain, Ph.D. • Отслеживаете
text: Lt. Gen. Joseph Jarrard, deputy commander of NORTHCOM, said this month: "We don't have the sensors... We are ill-equipped right now to handle something like that... We're seeing it used on a daily basis around the world, and we've got to figure out how to mitigate that threat. But we're not there yet." He also separately said: "Detection is obviously the biggest issue, and so how we are able to detect is one of our biggest concerns right now." Meanwhile, the counter-drone vendor pitch for 2026 is almost uniformly "layered defense" — stack an RF detector, an AI-video classifier, a kinetic or non-kinetic effector, and call it depth. Several recent product launches lead with AI video fused to RF as the differentiator. Here's the disconnect. A three-star just told the public the bottleneck is sensors and detection, not effector diversity. And detection at swarm tempo isn't really a sensor-count problem — it's a track-correlation problem. Every additional modality is another stream that has to be time-aligned, classified, and reconciled with the others before anyone can act. Add a sensor without solving fusion latency and false-positive suppression, and you've made the decision harder, not easier, against a swarm that's inside your OODA loop in single-digit seconds. If you're building in this space, the question worth obsessing over isn't "what's my next sensor modality." It's "how fast and how reliably does my fusion engine resolve conflicting tracks into one actionable picture" — because that's the gap NORTHCOM's own leadership is naming publicly, not a gap in sensor variety. Where do you think the real bottleneck is — sensor coverage, fusion latency, or engagement authority? #DoW #Defense #Autonomy #CUAS
author: Sachin Jain, Ph.D. • Отслеживаете
